story.headline: Oil fell about 6% to near $110 a barrel as Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish envoys met Iran's leaders to head off new fighting. Currencies barely moved ahead of five central-bank decisions this week.

reads.policy: Five central banks decide this week, and most still lean toward raising rates because energy keeps inflation high. Canada and New Zealand are expected to hike; the Fed, the ECB and the Bank of Japan are expected to hold. Falling oil makes the case for more hikes a little weaker everywhere.
reads.growth: Monday's surveys were better than feared. German firms are more hopeful about the months ahead, UK retailers saw sales fall far less than expected, and US activity ran slightly above its normal pace. None of it moved currencies much before a week full of central-bank decisions.
reads.inflation: Energy is still the main reason inflation runs above target in most big economies. Monday's drop in oil helps a little, but central banks will want to see it last. Australia's inflation figures on Tuesday evening, CT, are the week's first big test of that.
reads.risk: Markets calmed as diplomats went to Tehran and the weekend passed without new US strikes. That cut demand for safe places to park money, so the yen eased a little. Fresh attacks or failed talks would quickly reverse that.
reads.tot: Oil fell sharply as regional envoys pressed Iran to avoid new fighting. That helps big energy importers like Japan and the euro area and takes some support away from Canada. The drop has not yet moved those currencies much.
reads.positioning: Hedge funds are betting most heavily against the Canadian dollar and the kiwi, even though both central banks are expected to hike this week, so those bets are exposed if the hikes come with signals of more. In the pound and the Aussie, hedge funds and long-term investors take opposite sides.
reads.fiscal: Pressure on France eased after Moody's held its rating, which helped the euro early on Monday. Britain's first Budget from Chancellor Healey on Wednesday is now the bigger test: heavier borrowing could unsettle UK bonds and the pound.

fed.summary: The Federal Reserve is expected to hold rates on Wednesday and raise them in December, because high oil keeps US inflation up. Monday's fall in oil eases that pressure a little.
fed.priced: October: hold expected; December: hike likely.
fed.why: Energy-driven inflation is still above the Fed's comfort zone and the economy is growing a little faster than normal. Cheaper oil, if it lasts, would weaken the case for a December hike.
fed.watch: The decision at 1:00 PM CT Wednesday and the press conference at 1:30 PM CT. A hold is priced; the surprise would be a clear push toward or away from a December hike.

boc.summary: The Bank of Canada is expected to raise rates on Wednesday because energy is pushing Canadian inflation above its forecasts. Much of that is already in the loonie's price, and a few banks now expect a hold.
boc.why: Governor Tiff Macklem has warned that energy will push inflation well above the bank's forecasts, and Canadian spending has held up. Falling oil and US tariffs argue for caution.
boc.watch: The decision and Monetary Policy Report at 8:45 AM CT Wednesday. A hold would be the surprise; a hike with a signal of more would be the stronger outcome for the loonie.

rbnz.summary: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand is expected to raise rates at 8:00 PM CT on Tuesday, because inflation is still above its target. That expectation supports the kiwi.
rbnz.why: Inflation cooled only slightly in the third quarter and stays above the bank's target band, so the case for a hike held.
rbnz.watch: The decision on Tuesday evening, CT, and whether the bank signals more hikes after this one.

ecb.summary: The European Central Bank is expected to hold on Thursday and lean toward a hike in December, as energy keeps euro-area inflation high. Moody's decision to spare France has eased one worry for the euro.
ecb.priced: October 29: hold expected; December: hike likely.
ecb.why: Energy keeps inflation above the ECB's target, and German business surveys keep improving. France's debt troubles are the main reason to go carefully.
ecb.watch: The decision at 8:15 AM CT Thursday and President Christine Lagarde's press conference, especially anything on French bonds or a December hike.

boj.summary: The Bank of Japan is expected to hold on Friday, but a December hike is widely expected now that inflation is back above its 2% goal. The yen needs that hike, or a clear signal of it, to recover.
boj.priced: October 30: hold expected; December: hike likely.
boj.why: Inflation is above the bank's goal and spreading beyond fuel, which strengthens the case for higher rates.
boj.watch: Tokyo consumer prices on Wednesday evening, CT, then the decision and new forecasts on Friday, Japan time.

rba.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia may raise rates on November 3, and markets see it as close to an even bet. Tuesday evening's inflation figures will likely decide it.
rba.priced: November 3: about an even chance of a hike.
rba.why: Its officials say the inflation job is not done, but weak business surveys make another hike a harder call.
rba.watch: Australia's third-quarter inflation figures at 7:30 PM CT Tuesday: a hot reading makes a November hike likely.

boe.summary: The Bank of England is all but certain to raise rates on November 5 after UK inflation came in hotter than expected. Wednesday's Budget will shape whether a second hike follows.
boe.priced: November 5: hike almost certain; December: open.
boe.why: Inflation is running well above target, driven by energy. Weak shoppers argued for caution, but Monday's retail survey was far better than feared.
boe.watch: Chancellor Healey's Budget on Wednesday morning, CT: how much the government borrows and spends feeds into the bank's next steps.

snb.summary: The Swiss National Bank holds rates at zero because Swiss inflation is near zero. Global fear, not Swiss policy, sets the franc's path.
snb.priced: December 10: no change expected, with a small chance of a cut.
snb.why: Swiss inflation is close to zero and producer prices are soft, so the bank has no reason to tighten and some reason to worry about a strong franc.
snb.watch: Any comment on the strong franc from board members, and the December 10 decision.

USD.summary: The dollar has among the highest rates of the major currencies, with a Federal Reserve hike expected in December. Falling oil on Monday eased the inflation worry behind that, leaving the dollar slightly softer.

notes.policy: The Fed is expected to hold on Wednesday and hike in December, which supports the dollar.
notes.inflation: High oil keeps US inflation well above the Fed's goal, though Monday's drop eases that a little.

EUR.summary: The euro is held back by weak business surveys, France's debt troubles and heavy energy costs, though Moody's sparing France and an expected ECB hike in December help.

notes.policy: The ECB is expected to hold this week, so the hike case for December offers less near-term lift than rivals' moves.
notes.growth: Euro-area business surveys missed in October, although German firms are more hopeful about the months ahead.
notes.inflation: Energy keeps euro-area inflation high, which keeps a December ECB hike on the table.
notes.tot: The euro area imports most of its energy, so high oil drains money out of the region.
notes.positioning: Hedge funds have added to bets against the euro, which can fuel sharp rises if the news improves.
notes.fiscal: France's debt and budget fight weigh on the euro, even after Moody's held its rating.

GBP.summary: The pound is supported by a Bank of England hike that is all but certain for November 5 and by hot inflation, but Wednesday's UK Budget adds caution.

notes.policy: A Bank of England hike on November 5 is all but priced, which supports the pound.
notes.growth: UK business surveys and Monday's retail survey were better than feared.
notes.inflation: UK inflation is running well above target, which keeps the hike case strong.

JPY.summary: The yen sits low on the board because Japan's rates are still far below others' and the country pays for costly imported energy, though a December Bank of Japan hike is widely expected.

notes.policy: Japan's rates are still well below other major economies', so holding yen pays little.
notes.risk: The yen gains when markets get nervous, which helped it last week.
notes.tot: Japan imports nearly all its energy, so high oil weighs on the yen, though Monday's drop helps.

CHF.summary: The franc is pulled between near-zero Swiss inflation, which keeps rates at zero, and its role as a safe place for money when markets are nervous.

notes.inflation: Swiss inflation is near zero, which leaves the Swiss National Bank no reason to raise rates.
notes.risk: The franc gains when investors look for safety, which has kept it near recent highs.

AUD.summary: The Aussie is supported by a central bank that may hike again in November, but weak business surveys hold it back. Tuesday evening's inflation figures will likely decide its next move.

notes.policy: The Reserve Bank of Australia may raise rates on November 3, which supports the Aussie.
notes.growth: Australia's private sector shrank in October for the first time in five months.
notes.tot: Australia exports energy and raw materials, so high commodity prices bring money in, though Monday's oil drop trims that a little.

CAD.summary: The loonie is near its strongest in a month on a likely Bank of Canada hike this Wednesday and high oil, though Monday's oil drop and US tariffs are headwinds.

notes.policy: A Bank of Canada hike on Wednesday is mostly expected, which supports the loonie.
notes.growth: Canada's economy is still soft, and US tariffs weigh on its exporters.
notes.inflation: Energy is pushing Canadian inflation above the central bank's forecasts.
notes.tot: As an oil exporter, Canada gains from high prices, so Monday's drop takes some support away.

NZD.summary: The kiwi sits near the top of the board because New Zealand's central bank is expected to raise rates on Tuesday evening, CT, and its services sector keeps growing.

notes.policy: A Reserve Bank of New Zealand hike is widely expected this week, which supports the kiwi.
notes.growth: New Zealand's services sector has grown for four straight months, giving the central bank room to raise rates.
notes.risk: The kiwi has held firm this month on the rate-hike bets, though it still drops when stocks fall.
notes.tot: Firm dairy prices, New Zealand's biggest export, bring money into the country.
